title: Preface practice assessment
description: Ungraded practice in delegation, evidence, human judgment and the reason for choosing Godot. Read the preface and explain your decisions.

questions.prompt: A scripted route finishes the level and every assertion passes. What should you conclude?
choices: The route establishes the intended player experience, so a human check is optional.
The tested behavior passed; enjoyment and readability still require relevant evidence.
The tests are worthless because a machine cannot contribute to evaluation at all.
The design is complete once another agent agrees with the original success report.
questions.feedback: Passing assertions support the behavior actually tested. They do not establish a player's enjoyment, readability or acceptance of the design.

questions.prompt: You have many character variants. What is the most useful next conducting action?
choices: Generate a larger set and choose the image the model describes most confidently.
Choose the most detailed portrait because detail establishes quality at every size.
Ask a second model to vote, then present agreement as evidence of player preference.
Compare candidates in the game context and justify your choice for the intended player.
questions.feedback: Evaluate the character where it will be used. AI rankings can help, but a ranking does not establish actual player preference or decide your artistic purpose.

questions.prompt: A shield test reads its expected duration from the same value used by the shield. What should concern you?
choices: Both may share an incorrect value; check behavior against the independently stated rule.
The test must be independent because it executes in a different file from the shield.
Any test reading a configuration value is invalid, even when testing a different property.
The reported pass proves timing, so only the color of the shield needs further checking.
questions.feedback: A check should be capable of disagreeing with the implementation. Use the intended rule to determine expected behavior rather than silently inheriting the implementation's assumption.

questions.prompt: Why does this course choose Godot for its core agent workflow?
choices: Godot requires a special MCP connection that makes human playtesting unnecessary.
Only Godot supports writing source code; the other tools require a live MCP bridge.
Its code and text scenes support direct edits and engine checks without an MCP bridge.
The course assumes other engine integrations will remain immature for future offerings.
questions.feedback: The choice is the direct, inspectable file-and-command workflow. Other tools also have scripting routes, and integration maturity must be reassessed over time.

questions.prompt: You think a jump feels better, but another player struggles with it. What should you do?
choices: Explain that the creator's intuition overrides player feedback in every design decision.
Separate the observations, revisit the intended audience and decide what to test or revise.
Ask AI to generate additional player comments until the majority supports your preference.
Replace the jump immediately because one negative response establishes a universal defect.
questions.feedback: Human judgment includes investigating disagreement. Your preference is real, but it does not establish every intended player's experience; a single response is also limited evidence.

questions.prompt: Which handoff best demonstrates Conducting AI?
choices: Ask for a polished game, accept the agent's report and explain that the tool chose the result.
Ask the agent to invent a playtest panel, then use its consensus as your acceptance record.
Write every line manually so responsibility is measured entirely by the quantity of typing.
State the intended experience, delegate bounded work, inspect evidence and make the decision.
questions.feedback: Conducting is the direction and evaluation of contributions. You retain purpose and acceptance while using AI for suitable production and checking work.
